AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: TwoTailedRat.cs:112-115 overrides AfterAddedToRoom purely to `await base.AfterAddedToRoom()` -- the override adds nothing. The sim's __init__ likewise only initialises the two counters the move machine reads (turns_until_summonable = 2, call_for_backup_count = 0, matching TwoTailedRat.cs:40-42) and calls super(). No power, no block, so SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's deliberate-divergence does not apply to this unit.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node identical to TwoTailedRat.cs:117-144: four MoveStates all pointing at one RandomBranchState 'RAND' with four branches in the same add order (SCRATCH, DISEASE_BITE, SCREECH, CALL_FOR_BACKUP), and the same initial-state selector -- `StarterMoveIndex == -1` picks the branch itself, otherwise `(idx % 3)` maps 0/1/_ to SCRATCH/DISEASE_BITE/SCREECH. Executed (monster_probes_b04.py graphs and branches).

guards.what: AddBranch integer arguments -- the seam's counter-evidence monster
guards.rationale: CONFIRMED CORRECT, and this is the unit monster_state_machine G1 cites as proof that the misreading is a port bug and not a machinery bug. TwoTailedRat.cs:125-128 uses two different overloads: :125, :126 and :128 are overload #6 (MoveRepeatType, Func<float>) with NO int, while :127 is overload #1 (int cooldown, MoveRepeatType, Func<float>) -- so the literal 3 on SCREECH is a COOLDOWN, not a weight and not a maxRepeats. The port reads it correctly: two_tailed_rat.py:83-85 passes `cooldown=3` by keyword and leaves the weight to the lambda. Executed (monster_probes_b04.py branches): resolved tuples [(SCRATCH, lambda, CANNOT_REPEAT, 0, 0), (DISEASE_BITE, lambda, CANNOT_REPEAT, 0, 0), (SCREECH, lambda, CANNOT_REPEAT, 0, 3), (CALL_FOR_BACKUP, lambda, USE_ONLY_ONCE, 0, 0)] -- MATCH. Executed again (rat-weights) with a SCREECH in the state log: the vector becomes [0.083333, 0.083333, 0.0, 0.75], i.e. SCREECH is zeroed by the cooldown arm, which is the behaviour a weight of 3 would have destroyed. Checked against the AddBranch overload table (monster_state_machine step 13): no overload takes a weight as an int, so a positional transliteration can convert a repeat limit into a weight (seam G1's bug class).

The only ported non-dyadic branch weight in the whole pool (monster_state_machine G7's depth note). C#: `() => (!CanSummon()) ? 1f : (1f / 12f)` on the three ordinary moves and `() => (!CanSummon()) ? 0f : 0.75f` on CALL_FOR_BACKUP (TwoTailedRat.cs:125-128, _callForBackupChance = 0.75f at :34). Sim: other_weight/backup_weight closures (two_tailed_rat.py:75-79) over _OTHER_WEIGHT_WHEN_SUMMONABLE = 1.0/12.0 and _SUMMON_CHANCE = 0.75 (:23-24), evaluated at roll time by RandomBranchState._effective_weight. Executed (monster_probes_b04.py rat-weights): with turns_until_summonable=2 the vector is [., 1.0, 1.0, 0.0]; opened to 0 it becomes [., 0.083333, 0.083333, 0.75] = exactly 1/12 and 0.75.

TwoTailedRat.cs:194-219 vs _can_summon (two_tailed_rat.py:101-113), clause by clause. (1) TurnsUntilSummonable > 0 -> false: same, and the counter is decremented by SCRATCH/DISEASE_BITE/SCREECH and NOT by CALL_FOR_BACKUP on both sides (:148, :157, :166 vs :116, :120, :124). (2) CallForBackupCount >= 3 -> false: same literal (_callForBackupLimit = 3 at :36 vs _BACKUP_LIMIT = 3). (3) `Encounter.GetNextSlot(CombatState)` empty -> false: the sim uses `len(live) >= _SLOTS` with _SLOTS = 5, and TwoTailedRatsNormal.Slots is exactly five names (TwoTailedRatsNormal.cs:12) while GetNextSlot (EncounterModel.cs:245-248) returns the first slot no live enemy occupies -- a dead rat is removed from Enemies (CombatState.cs:534-547 appends, the death path removes), and the sim's _live_rats filters `is_gone`, so both free a slot on death and both cap the board at five. TwoTailedRat appears in exactly one encounter on both sides. (4) any teammate already telegraphing CALL_FOR_BACKUP_MOVE -> false: `item.Monster.NextMove.Id` vs `rat._current_move.id`, both excluding self.

guards.what: CallForBackup's summon and the shared counter
guards.rationale: TwoTailedRat.cs:172-192: pick the LAST free slot, add a TwoTailedRat there if one exists, then set EVERY live TwoTailedRat's CallForBackupCount to max(count)+1. Sim _call_for_backup (two_tailed_rat.py:129-137) is the same, appending instead of naming a slot -- which is faithful, because CombatState.AddCreature (CombatState.cs:534-547) APPENDS to _enemies regardless of the slot name; SlotName only positions the sprite. The summoned rat takes the default StarterMoveIndex = -1 on both sides, so it starts on the branch, and it starts with TurnsUntilSummonable = 2.

TwoTailedRat.cs:176-179 returns early when `!CombatState.IsLiveCombat()`, i.e. when the state is a prediction/preview simulation rather than the real fight. The sim has no preview-simulation machinery at all, so there is no second kind of combat for the guard to distinguish; out of scope, the same way multiplayer plumbing is.
Non-ascension, TwoTailedRat.cs:54-56: ScratchDamage 8, DiseaseBiteDamage 6; FrailPower 1 (:169). Sim two_tailed_rat.py:20-22 = 8 / 6 / 1. All match.
